tasks.gr12-two-dimensional-arrays-t2: Topic: Two-dimensional arrays in Delphi for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 2 programming). Cover the structure of a 2-D array (rows and columns, declared with array[1..R, 1..C] of a type, indexed as arr[row, column], one data type, bounds that count from 1), stepping through the elements with nested loops (the outer loop for the rows and the inner loop for the columns, row by row), basic operations such as row and column totals and the grand total (reset the total to 0 for each row or column; local variables are not set to 0 automatically), finding the largest value and its position, counting values that meet a condition, integer division with div and mod, and common errors (a total that is not reset, a reset in the wrong place, swapped indexes, an index outside the declared bounds). Every number in a question must be worked out from the array shown; ask learners to read and trace code and to give the result.
tasks.gr12-hardware-mobile-technologies-t1: Topic: Hardware: mobile technologies and performance for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 1 systems technologies). Cover mobile technologies (smart phones, laptops, tablets, netbooks, e-book readers), the advantages of mobility, the constraints (battery life, size, computing power against power consumption), the factors that influence the performance of a computer (CPU speed and multi-processing, memory capacity: cache and RAM, storage speed, network speed), and how to motivate a typical computer system for a purpose (home or personal use, games and entertainment, SOHO, power user) by linking the need to the hardware. State performance facts relatively, without fixed figures. Ask definitions, comparisons and motivation questions.
tasks.gr12-software-methodologies-design-tools: Topic: Software methodologies and design tools for Grade 12 Information Technology (CAPS Term 1 software engineering principles and the start of the PAT). Cover and compare the waterfall, rapid application development (RAD), incremental and agile methodologies (idea, strength, weakness and the situation each suits), the design tools TOE (Task, Objects, Events), IPO (Input, Process, Output), CRC cards (Class, Responsibilities, Collaborators) and UML (use case diagram and basic class diagram), noun-verb analysis (nouns suggest classes and attributes, verbs suggest methods), and using a methodology to analyse the requirements at the start of the PAT. Present the methodologies fairly: none is best for every project. Ask comparison and application questions.
